changes_vs_current: New topic. Ranked by average position over 6 people sources (missing = list length + 5). Raw order: Harvard 4.0, Stanford 4.8, Yale 6.0, Princeton 6.8, MIT 7.8, Michigan 9.3, Duke 9.3, Berkeley 11.5, Columbia 11.7, Cornell 13.0, Penn 13.2, UCLA 13.3, Notre Dame 13.5, Brown 13.8, NYU 15.7, Texas A&M 15.7, UT Austin 16.5, Ohio State 17.3, Penn State 17.3, BYU 18.2, Northwestern 18.7, USC 18.7, Purdue 19.3, Georgetown 19.5, then Dartmouth, JHU, UChicago, UNC. Gut-check moves: UCLA 12 to 10 (gut top-6, in 4 sources, #8 fan base, most applications of any US school); Notre Dame 13 to 11 (6th in Gallup open-ended, big football profile); Ohio State 18 to 12 (largest college football fan base, 13th in Gallup; only pageviews put it low); USC 22 to 17 (gut top-10, 16th in pageviews; held at 17 because Gallup had 1% and it is missing from YouGov top 20 and both dream-school lists); Alabama (outside raw top 30) inserted at 21 (6th in fan base, gut pick; held low as it is missing from YouGov and Gallup and low in pageviews). BYU (raw 20) and Purdue (raw 23) dropped for Alabama and Johns Hopkins (raw 26, YouGov fame 86%). Penn and Penn State are separate items; OSU is used only on Ohio State; bare 'UT' left out (Tennessee/Utah).
confidence: High for the top 7 (Harvard, Stanford, Yale, Princeton, MIT, Michigan, Duke). Medium for 8-17: Ivy vs big public order depends on whether a source measures prestige or sports fandom. Low-medium for 18-24. Near misses: BYU, Purdue, Dartmouth, UChicago, UNC, Florida State, Georgia, West Point, Caltech, Vanderbilt, UVA, LSU, Florida. Caveats: Gallup is from 2003; YouGov shows only its top 20 and uses full names (undercounts MIT, maybe UCLA/USC); the fan-base source counts sports fans only; pageviews are news-inflated (Brown); the two Princeton Review lists come from one applicant-heavy survey.
